Subject: Question on import onboarding and amortization options

Hi Sofia,

Quick follow-up from our security and procurement sync this morning — thank you for walking us through the residency options. Two narrow questions from our side as we prepare the PO:

1) For onboarding historical PHI into the customer-controlled KMS/HSM environment and the auditlog migration, do you treat that as a one-time implementation fee or as a creditable cost that can be amortized against committed spend?
2) If credited/amortized, what cadence and lookback do you normally use (monthly credit over 12 months, quarterly, etc.)?

Corus is trying to avoid a big up-front invoice if we can reasonably amortize implementation costs against a 12–18 month commit. We also need the cost split between the KMS/HSM provisioning, the audit log ingestion work, and the residency activation itself for our internal chargeback.

Can you send a short proposal with numbers (ballpark is fine) and any contract language you recommend? We have a purchasing deadline of Dec 21.

Thanks — Jordan

Hi Jordan — great questions, and totally understand the desire to avoid a large one-time hit. Below are two standard paths we offer plus a hybrid that has worked well for other health systems. Attaching a short sample SOW and an evidence manifest for reference.

Option A — One-time onboarding fee (simpler billing)
- Flat fee to cover auditlog ingestion, PHI import runbooks, and KMS/HSM seat activation.
- Typical range for a setup like Corus (50M tokens/month baseline + 30TB auditlog import): $22,000–$35,000 one-time.
- Invoice at activation; no amortization.

Option B — Amortized credit against committed spend
- We convert the implementation fee into a monthly credit applied to invoice over a defined term.
- Common terms: 12 months (most), 18 months (for multi-year pilots).
- Example: $30k implementation -> $2.5k/month credit over 12 months, applied as an invoice line-item.

Option C — Hybrid (reduced upfront + shorter amortization)
- Split upfront (50%) + 6–12 month credit on the remainder. This reduces initial cashflow while keeping programmatic commitment.

Notes/contract language we suggest to include in SOW:
- Scope bucketing (auditlog ingest vs residency region vs KMS seats) with line-item estimates.
- Credit application: explicit monthly credit line referencing the Deal ID.
- Evidence delivery milestones (attestation, manifest CSV, transfer checklist).

If you like, I can propose a specific commercial callout — e.g., $28k total, $14k upfront invoice + $14k credited over 7 months ($2k/mo). That would leave a modest up-front PO and a predictable run-rate impact.

Next steps: which path looks closest to Corus' procurement preference? If you want Ben/Revenue on quick pricing validation I can loop them in.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Pricing ask — Corus Health (DEAL-4321) — onboarding credit vs fee

Team — looping you in for quick guidance before I send final commercial language to Corus procurement. Summary below from the Corus ask:
- Expected baseline: ~50M tokens/month, residency in us-west, auditlog backfill ~30TB.
- Customer preference: avoid large upfront invoice; would prefer amortized credit over 12–18 months.
- They need line items by scope for chargeback (KMS seat provisioning, HSM attestation, auditlog ingest).

My proposed commercial options to present (ballpark):
1) Straight one-time fee: $28,000 (covers everything).
2) Amortized credit: convert $28k -> $2,333/month credit over 12 months.
3) Hybrid: $14k upfront + $14k credited over 7 months ($2k/mo).

We should consider offering a small concession to close this before 12/21. My recommendation: authorize up to a 15% concession on the total implementation amount if needed (i.e., max discount down to ~$23.8k). If we approve the hybrid we can reduce cash friction and still protect unit economics.

Questions for you:
- Ben: ok to approve up to 15% concession on implementation fees for a US health system with a 12–18 month commit?
- Jonas: do we have any concerns about applying credits to hosted usage invoices (accounting/recognition)? If there's an approval path required, please advise.

Thanks — will hold any external follow-up until I get greenlight.

— Sofia
